A surreal mixed media composition centers on a grayscale figure seated in a simple upholstered chair, their posture withdrawn with hands clasped tightly in their lap. Their entire head has been replaced by an enormous human eye that stares directly outward, creating an unsettling focal point. Surrounding the eye is a chaotic mass of crumpled newspaper pages, layered into a circular form like a distorted halo or exploding thought cloud. Thick crimson paint is smeared across the newspapers and the eyelids, then splatters outward in violent streaks and drips heavily downward, contrasting sharply against the otherwise monochrome scene. Black ink splashes and paint marks scatter across the textured concrete wall behind the subject, adding to the feeling of disorder. The floor is littered with discarded newspaper pages, stained with pools and splashes of black paint. The restrained grayscale palette, interrupted only by vivid red, creates a striking visual metaphor for relentless media, observation, and psychological pressure while maintaining a raw collage aesthetic filled with torn textures, wrinkles, stains, and expressive brushwork.

A dramatic abstract painting centers on a weathered human skull emerging from a deep black background. Thick, expressive brushstrokes and palette knife textures create an explosion of white, crimson, coral, charcoal, and muted blue across the upper half of the skull, making it appear as though fragments of paint, ash, and flame are erupting from its crown. Empty eye sockets stare forward beneath splashes of dripping pigment, while streaks of red trail down the cheekbones and jaw. A lit cigarette rests between the skull's teeth, its glowing ember sending a delicate ribbon of pale smoke curling toward the right side of the composition. Rising from the darkness below, a skeletal hand extends toward the viewer with two fingers raised in a peace sign. The fingers are rendered with cracked bone, layered paint, and rough texture that echo the skull above. The background fades between smoky gray and black with energetic splatters, scratches, drips, and exposed canvas, emphasizing the raw, expressive style. The overall composition balances decay with defiance, combining painterly chaos and bold contrast into a striking contemporary horror-inspired artwork.

🔬 Generative AI could support critical-care prediction and documentation, while ethics, bias and oversight remain central. @embo.org
#CriticalCare #GenerativeAI
🔗 www.xiahepublishing.com/2590-3438/JT...

external.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and multimodal systems, is emerging as a potentially important innovation in intensive care medicine. The intensive care unit (ICU) is a data-dense, high-acuity setting where rapid and accurate decisions are critical. These models can translate complex multimodal data into interpretable and clinically actionable insights across diagnostic, prognostic, and documentation workflows. This review outlines six key domains in which generative AI is currently being explored for its potential to reshape critical care: clinical decision support; clinical documentation automation (AI scribe, voice-to-note); predictive analytics, including sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome prediction, acute kidney injury management, ventilator liberation readiness, delirium monitoring, and continuous renal replacement therapy optimization; ICU data summarization and multimodal monitoring; synthetic data generation; and legal and ethical governance. In clinical decision support, hybrid models that integrate time-series monitoring data with LLMs can contextualize alerts, generate diagnostic suggestions, and offer treatment plans with explainable reasoning. Documentation tools that leverage ambient listening and voice-to-note AI can streamline progress notes and discharge summaries, thereby reducing clinician workload. In predictive analytics, LLMs enhance model performance by augmenting sparse electronic health record data and translating outputs into interpretable narratives. Synthetic data generation enables algorithm development and training, particularly for rare events, while protecting patient privacy. However, the realism and ethical deployment of such data require rigorous validation. Widespread implementation of generative AI will require careful attention to challenges related to trust, validation, bias, liability, and regulatory compliance. The use of these tools must remain under clinician supervision to ensure transparency and accountability. With responsible deployment, generative AI may augment ICU workflows, improve outcomes, and reduce clinician burden, potentially becoming an indispensable component of critical care delivery.
external.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care Medicine: A Narrative Review of Applications, Predictive Analytics, Documentation, and Ethical Imperatives

🔬 A posterior transosseous S1 pedicle route is proposed as an alternative way to access the superior hypogastric plexus. @cp-cancercell.bsky.social
#PainMedicine #InterventionalRadiology
🔗 www.xiahepublishing.com/2472-0712/ER...

external.description: Chronic pelvic pain remains a significant clinical challenge, often refractory to conservative and interventional treatments. Superior hypogastric plexus block is an established technique; however, conventional anterior and posterior approaches may be limited by anatomical variability and potential risks to adjacent structures. Based on these anatomical findings, we propose that a posterior transosseous S1 pedicular approach represents a novel and anatomically robust corridor for accessing the superior hypogastric plexus. We hypothesize that the highly reproducible osseous anatomy of the S1 pedicle, combined with its consistent spatial relationship to the anterior sacral cortex and retroperitoneal compartment, may enable precise and fluoroscopically reproducible instrument guidance toward the plexus. Furthermore, this trajectory may mitigate the anatomical variability and procedural limitations associated with conventional anterior or paravertebral techniques while potentially reducing the risk of inadvertent injury to adjacent visceral, vascular, and neural structures. This concept is based on anatomical reasoning and fluoroscopic observations obtained during cadaveric anatomical orientation, suggesting that a transosseous trajectory through the S1 pedicle toward the anterior sacral cortex may offer improved spatial control and reproducibility compared with soft-tissue-based approaches. The proposed pathway remains conceptual and is not intended for clinical application at this stage. Further cadaveric, imaging-based, and clinical studies are required to evaluate its anatomical validity, safety, and potential clinical relevance.
external.title: A Posterior Transosseous S1 Pedicle Approach for Accessing the Superior Hypogastric Plexus: A Hypothesis
